sequences.title: Build a savings sequence
sequences.intro: Change the first weekly deposit and the fixed increase. Compare the nth deposit with the total saved. This is an arithmetic sequence with no interest.
sequences.challenge: With first deposit 10 and increase 5, what is the total deposited over 10 weeks?
sequences.working: S₁₀ = 10/2 × [2(10) + 9(5)] = 325. The tenth deposit alone is 55.

interest.title: Compare compound and simple growth
interest.intro: Explore a fictional savings account with annual compounding and no fees, tax or additional deposits. Mint is compound growth; gold is simple growth.
interest.challenge: At 5% compounded annually, what is a balance of 1000 worth after 2 years?
interest.working: 1000 × 1.05² = 1102.50. Apply each year's increase to the updated balance.

loan.title: Step through a loan
loan.intro: Use a fictional loan with monthly interest followed by an end-of-month payment. Advance one month at a time. Changing a control starts a new loan; fees are omitted.
loan.challenge: A debt of 5000 accrues 0.5% monthly interest, then a payment of 200 is made. What balance remains?

line.title: Fit a straight-line model
line.intro: Adjust slope and intercept to fit the three gold data points. Interpret slope as change in y for one unit of x. The points are fictional observations.
line.challenge: For a taxi model C = 2d + 3, find the cost for d = 8 km.
line.working: C = 2(8) + 3 = 19. The intercept is the starting charge; the slope is cost per kilometre.

quadratic.title: Move a quadratic vertex
quadratic.intro: Explore y = a(x − h)² + k. Move the vertex and change the curvature. The displayed domain is −6 ≤ x ≤ 6.
quadratic.challenge: For y = 2(x − 3)² + 4, what is the minimum y-value?
quadratic.working: The squared term is non-negative and a is positive. The minimum occurs at x = 3 and equals 4.

triangle.title: Measure an inaccessible height
triangle.intro: Move the observation point and angle of elevation. The model assumes level ground and adds the observer's eye height. Angles are in degrees.
triangle.challenge: At horizontal distance 20 m and elevation angle 45°, with eye height 1.5 m, find the total height.
triangle.working: Height = 20 tan(45°) + 1.5 = 21.5 m. The horizontal distance is the adjacent side.

voronoi.title: Move a service centre
voronoi.intro: Move centre B across the map. Coloured regions show which of two service centres is closer in straight-line distance. The query point is fixed at (5, 6); centre A is at (2, 5).
voronoi.challenge: What is the distance between A(2, 5) and B(8, 5)?
voronoi.working: The points share a y-coordinate, so the distance is |8 − 2| = 6. The two-site Voronoi boundary is the perpendicular bisector.

statistics.title: Change a data set
statistics.intro: Edit a small data set to see how an outlier changes the mean, median and standard deviation. Enter 2–30 finite numbers separated by commas; each must be between −1000 and 1000.
statistics.working: The ordered list has five values. The third is 4. The mean is 7, which is more affected by the large value.

regression.title: Watch an outlier change regression
regression.intro: Move the final y-value in a five-point data set. Compare the least-squares line and Pearson's r. Association alone is not evidence of causation.
regression.challenge: A fitted model is y = 2x + 1. What is its predicted y-value at x = 4?
regression.working: y = 2(4) + 1 = 9. Predictions far outside the observed x-range may be unreliable.

binomial.title: Experiment with a binomial model
binomial.intro: Change n and p, then simulate batches of independent trials with the same success probability. Bars show exact probabilities; the simulation shows sampling variability.
binomial.challenge: For three independent fair coin tosses, what is P(exactly two heads)?
binomial.working: There are three ways to get two heads, each with probability (0.5)³. The total is 3/8 = 0.375.

normal.title: Move a normal-distribution cutoff
normal.intro: Adjust a mean, standard deviation and cutoff. The shaded area estimates P(X ≤ cutoff). This is a continuous model; the probability at one exact point is zero.
normal.challenge: For any normal distribution, what is P(X ≤ the mean)?
normal.working: The normal density is symmetric about its mean, with half of its total area on either side.

tangent.title: Turn a secant into a tangent
tangent.intro: For f(x) = x², move the point and reduce the horizontal gap h. Compare the secant slope with the derivative 2x. Gold is the secant; mint is the curve.
tangent.challenge: What is the gradient of y = x² at x = 3?
tangent.working: dy/dx = 2x, so the gradient at x = 3 is 6. A small secant interval approximates this limit.

trapezoids.title: Build a trapezoidal estimate
trapezoids.intro: Increase the number of equal strips under y = x² + 1 from x = 0 to x = 4. Compare the trapezoidal estimate with the exact integral. The function stays above the x-axis here.
trapezoids.challenge: Use one trapezoid to estimate the integral of y = x² + 1 from 0 to 4.
trapezoids.working: Width 4, endpoint heights 1 and 17: area ≈ 4(1 + 17)/2 = 36. The exact value is 76/3 ≈ 25.333.

optimization.title: Design a maximum-area enclosure
optimization.intro: Use 40 m of fencing for three sides of a rectangle against a straight wall. Change the width perpendicular to the wall and watch the area. No fencing is needed along the wall.
optimization.challenge: What width maximizes the area when 2w + l = 40?
optimization.working: A = w(40 − 2w), so A′ = 40 − 4w = 0 at w = 10 m. The length is 20 m and area is 200 m²; both endpoint areas are zero.
